clue.text: It preserves official notes to an evil personality

blocks.note: official as in formal, done by the book
two musical notes, D and E
Mr Hyde, the evil side of Dr Jekyll in Stevenson's story

explanation.surface: Someone's formal letters are written to a wicked character, and somehow those letters keep him going.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Notes' is plural, so it supplies two letter-names of the scale rather than one.
explanation.definitionFit: Formaldehyde is the chemical used to keep biological specimens and bodies from decaying, so it is a preservative.

clue.text: Father, like Uriah at heart, a poor catcher

indicators.note: what lies at the heart is in the middle, so the Dickensian word sits inside the abbreviation

blocks.note: Fr is the abbreviation for Father, a priest
Uriah Heep in Dickens's David Copperfield keeps calling himself 'umble'

explanation.surface: A priest, smarmy as Uriah Heep deep down, keeps dropping the ball.
explanation.walkthrough: Uriah Heep drops his aitches, so his 'humble' is spelt without the H.
explanation.definitionFit: A fumbler handles things clumsily, so in a ball game he is someone who fails to hold a catch.

clue.text: Arrest knight involved in crash

indicators.note: being involved in something means being caught up inside it

blocks.note: a crash or financial collapse is ruin
N is the chess notation for knight

explanation.surface: A knight caught up in a car accident ends up arrested.
explanation.definitionFit: To run in is an informal British phrasal verb for taking a suspect into police custody.

clue.text: Rebel is a northern chief? It's possible

indicators.note: a possible version is one of several arrangements, so the letters before it may be reordered

blocks.note: taken as written
N is the abbreviation for northern
arch as in chief, as in arch-enemy
the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether a northern leader could be a revolutionary.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark and 'It's possible' read as a hedge; in fact they mark the final letters for shuffling.
explanation.definitionFit: An anarchist rejects all government and authority, so he is a kind of rebel.

clue.text: Information from teacher initially replacing companion in 6

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word before it
replacing means one piece is taken out of 6 and another put in its place

blocks.note: the first letter of teacher
CH stands for Companion of Honour, a British order
the answer to 6 down

explanation.surface: A teacher stands in for a friend at a country retreat, and that is how the facts come out.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap the two-letter companion out of the Russian cottage at 6 and put the teacher's initial in its place.
explanation.definitionFit: Data are facts and figures collected for reference, which is to say information.

clue.text: Unpaid woman in house overlooking railway

blocks.note: HO is the abbreviation for house
a woman's name
RY is the abbreviation for railway

explanation.surface: A woman doing unpaid work lives in a house that looks down on the railway line.
explanation.definitionFit: An honorary post is held without a salary, for the honour alone, so it is unpaid.

clue.text: American lawyer has tea in a Russian cottage

blocks.note: a district attorney, an American public prosecutor
cha is an informal British word for tea

explanation.surface: A US attorney takes tea in a country cottage in Russia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Has' just puts the tea after the lawyer.
explanation.definitionFit: A dacha is a Russian country house or summer villa, the kind of second home many city dwellers keep.

clue.text: Work prolifically in art and make a random selection

blocks.note: first meaning: to sketch a great deal, read as two words
second meaning: the idiom for deciding by chance

explanation.walkthrough: The second meaning is the standard idiom; the first splits it into literal words, doing plenty of sketching.
explanation.definitionFit: To pick straws or names from a hat is the usual phrase for choosing by chance, while sketching plenty is the literal reading.

clue.text: Soft bed for a sportsman

blocks.note: p for piano, soft in music
a bed of rock or soil is a layer

explanation.surface: A comfortable mattress for an athlete.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bed' here is a geological stratum, not furniture.
explanation.definitionFit: A player is someone who takes part in a game, so any sportsman is one.

clue.text: Cocktail including whisky and \.(%

blocks.note: first meaning: the classic mixed drink of whisky, sweet vermouth and bitters
the scan of the newspaper is unreadable here, so the second meaning is lost; it most likely named the New York island

explanation.walkthrough: The end of this clue is unreadable in the 1991 newspaper scan. The first half defines the drink; 'and' probably led to a second meaning, likely the island the drink is named after.
explanation.definitionFit: A Manhattan is a well-known mixed drink made with rye or bourbon, sweet vermouth and bitters, so it is a whisky cocktail.

clue.text: Sounds like Dodgson's contribution to Christmas

indicators.note: says outright that the answer is spoken the same as the name in question, not spelt the same

blocks.note: Charles Dodgson wrote the Alice books under the pen-name Lewis Carroll

explanation.surface: The author of Alice is imagined adding something of his own to the Christmas festivities.
explanation.walkthrough: Dodgson's possessive stands for his pen-name, which the solver must know: he signed his books Lewis Carroll.
explanation.definitionFit: A carol is a festive song sung at Yuletide, so it is something offered towards the seasonal celebrations.

clue.text: Girl keeps rejected article? What folly

indicators.note: something rejected is sent back, so the word is read in the opposite direction
the girl keeps something inside her, so her name wraps around the other piece

blocks.note: a girl's name
the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A girl hangs on to a magazine piece that was turned down, and someone sighs at how silly that is.
explanation.definitionFit: Lunacy is utter foolishness, so an exclamation about folly is answered by naming such madness.

clue.text: General respect for the commercial theatre here

blocks.note: broad as in general, not detailed
as in 'in one respect' meaning 'in one way'

explanation.surface: A plea for wide public regard toward commercial stage shows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'General' looks like a military rank but is the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Broadway is the New York street whose name stands for the big money-making stage productions of America.

clue.text: Country policemen encompass its reversal

indicators.note: the clue itself asks for the word its to be read back to front
to encompass is to surround, so the police force's letters go around the other piece

blocks.note: the Royal Ulster Constabulary, Northern Ireland's police force in 1991
taken as written

explanation.surface: Rural police turn something of their own upside down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Country' is an adjective here, as in country manners, not a nation.
explanation.definitionFit: Rustic describes things of the countryside, so it is a synonym of the adjective use of country.

clue.text: Health enquiry in some quarters can cause a confrontation

indicators.note: the greeting sits inside the letters for points of the compass

blocks.note: quarters are compass points; here south, west and north
how do? asks after someone's health, as in how do you do

explanation.surface: Asking after someone's health can, in certain circles, start a row.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quarters' are the four compass points; only some of them are used, with the greeting after the first.
explanation.definitionFit: A showdown is a decisive final clash between opponents, a face-to-face confrontation.

clue.text: Concealed exit soldiers used after gin party

blocks.note: a gin is a snare or trap for animals
a do is a party
other ranks, the soldiers who are not officers

explanation.surface: Troops slip away through a hidden way out once the gin-fuelled party is over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gin' is not the drink but the old word for an animal trap; 'used after' puts the soldiers at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A trapdoor is a hinged panel in a floor or ceiling giving a hidden way out of a room.

clue.text: Holding more than one office makes us all prim

indicators.note: makes is read as forms or constructs, so the following letters are built into a new word

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Holding several jobs at once turns everyone rather starchy.
explanation.definitionFit: Pluralism is the practice, especially among clergy, of holding two or more posts or benefices at the same time.

clue.text: Provincial paper upholding Polish graduate?

indicators.note: the paper holds the rest inside it, and in a down clue holding up also lifts the polish word to read bottom to top

blocks.note: The Sun, a British tabloid newspaper
to polish is to rub
a Bachelor of Arts

explanation.surface: A regional newspaper backs a Polish university graduate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polish' is capitalised as the first word of a phrase, but it is the verb meaning shine, not the nationality.
explanation.definitionFit: Suburban means belonging to the outskirts and is used to mean narrow and unsophisticated, much like provincial.

clue.text: Verbal dismissal of racing spy causes a fight

blocks.note: the word you say to send someone away
a racing tout spies on horses in training and sells tips

explanation.surface: Sending away a spy at the racecourse provokes a brawl.
explanation.walkthrough: A tout, in British racing, is someone who watches horses in training to sell tips on them.
explanation.definitionFit: A shoot-out is a gun battle, so it is a kind of fight; the word also covers a deciding penalty contest.

clue.text: Places, say, to obtain spectacles

indicators.note: say asks for the word as spoken, so its sound matters rather than its spelling

blocks.note: sites are places

explanation.surface: Someone hunts for glasses at various locations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spectacles' suggests eyeglasses; here it means things worth seeing.
explanation.definitionFit: Sights are impressive things to look at, the same as spectacles in the sense of grand displays.

clue.text: Treasurer's pouch needs rand

blocks.note: a purse is a small money pouch
R is the abbreviation for the rand, South Africa's currency

explanation.surface: A treasurer's money bag needs some South African currency in it.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is read as 'is', so the treasurer is the answer rather than the owner of the pouch.
explanation.definitionFit: A purser is the officer on a ship who keeps the accounts and handles money, a shipboard treasurer.

clue.text: China head lost in garden area

indicators.note: losing the head means the first letter is dropped from the word

blocks.note: china is crockery, plates and cups

explanation.surface: A precious china ornament goes missing in the garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'China' is the dishes, not the country.
explanation.definitionFit: A rockery is a part of a garden built of stones and planted with alpines.

clue.text: Complaint involving a bad setback for this pleasure-seeker

indicators.note: a setback is a backward step, so the word bad goes the wrong way
the complaint involves the rest, holding it inside itself

blocks.note: gout is a painful complaint of the joints
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A medical condition causes real trouble for a person who lives for fun.
explanation.walkthrough: Only bad is turned round; the a stays in front of it, and both sit inside the complaint.
explanation.definitionFit: A gadabout is someone who flits from one social outing to the next in search of enjoyment.

clue.text: Wood uprooted when room for research is required

indicators.note: a plant pulled up is turned upside down, so in a down clue the words read from bottom to top

blocks.note: as in 'as I left' meaning 'when I left'
a laboratory

explanation.surface: A tree is torn up when a research laboratory needs space.
explanation.definitionFit: Balsa is a very light timber from a tropical American tree, much used for model-making.

clue.text: Language Alice translated after introduction to Gryphon

indicators.note: an introduction is the opening, so only the start of the creature's name is used
translating turns words into a different form, so the name's letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the opening letter of the Gryphon, a creature Alice meets in Wonderland
taken as written

explanation.surface: Lewis Carroll's heroine is translated into another tongue after meeting the Gryphon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' places the Gryphon's letter first.
explanation.definitionFit: Gaelic is the Celtic tongue of Ireland and Scotland, so it is an example of a language.

clue.text: Hear about king having no superfluous fat

indicators.note: having something means holding it, so the king goes inside

blocks.note: lean meat or a lean body has no spare fat
R for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: News reaches us of a monarch who is trim and fit.
explanation.definitionFit: To learn of something is to be told or informed of it, just as hearing about it.

clue.text: Upsetting note about love

indicators.note: upsetting means overturning, so in a down clue the letters are flipped to read upwards

blocks.note: so, or soh, is the fifth note of the sol-fa scale
re means about, concerning

explanation.surface: A distressing letter concerning romance.
explanation.definitionFit: Eros is the Greek god of desire, and his name is used for sexual love itself.

clue.text: It's used for drying fibres by the Spanish

blocks.note: tow is coarse flax or hemp fibre
el is 'the' in Spanish

explanation.surface: Something for drying made from Spanish fibres.
explanation.definitionFit: A towel is a cloth you rub yourself with after a bath, so its whole job is drying.

clue.text: Car a bride wrecked, causing obstruction

indicators.note: a wrecked thing lies broken in pieces, so these letters are scrambled into a new order

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A bride crashes the wedding car and it blocks the road.
explanation.definitionFit: A barricade is a barrier thrown across a road or door to block passage.

clue.text: Token payment from serious individual in my envelope

indicators.note: something placed in an envelope is wrapped by it, so the word my goes around the piece

blocks.note: earnest means serious
one individual
taken as written

explanation.surface: A sincere person tucks a small payment into an envelope.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the individual goes inside my; the serious word stands in front.
explanation.definitionFit: Earnest money is a deposit paid to show good faith in a deal, a token sum binding the bargain.
